title: API Design Best Practices
description: Learn resource naming, versioning, error handling, and pagination for microservices APIs.

data.text: Good API design makes services easy to use and evolve. This lesson covers resource naming, versioning strategies, error handling, and pagination patterns.

terms.definition: The convention for naming API endpoints using nouns, not verbs.
The practice of versioning APIs to allow evolution without breaking consumers.
A standard format (RFC 7807) for representing errors in HTTP APIs.
The practice of splitting large result sets into pages.

items: Content negotiation: Accept header with media type (most flexible)

data.text: Use appropriate HTTP status codes and consistent error formats. The Problem Details (RFC 7807) standard provides a consistent structure for errors.

items: Offset pagination: /products?page=2&size=20 (simple, but can be slow at scale)
Include total count and next/previous links in responses

Exercise: Design a REST API
data.description: Design a REST API for a library system with books, members, and loans.
steps: Design endpoints with proper HTTP methods
Design error responses using Problem Details
data.expectedOutcome: An OpenAPI specification with endpoints, pagination, and error handling

items.question: Why use nouns instead of verbs in URLs?
items.answer: Because HTTP methods already express the action. /products with GET, POST, PUT, DELETE is cleaner than /getProducts.

items.question: What is the best versioning strategy?
items.answer: URL versioning is simplest and most visible. Header versioning is cleaner but harder to debug.

items.question: How do I paginate large datasets?
items.answer: Use cursor pagination for large datasets. Offset pagination is simpler but slower for deep pages.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use nouns, plural, lowercase for resource naming
Use consistent error formats and proper status codes
data.takeaway: Good API design is about consistency, clarity, and evolvability.
